stemMd: Glucose is present in the filtrate entering a healthy nephron but normally absent from final urine. Which process explains this?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Conversion of all glucose to oxygen in the bladder

options.label: C
options.textMd: Secretion of all glucose from blood into urine

options.label: D
options.textMd: Removal of every water molecule from the filtrate

options.label: E
options.textMd: Failure of glucose to enter the filtrate

explanationMd: Small glucose molecules can be filtered, then transported back into blood through the tubule. Absence from final urine therefore does not mean absence from the initial filtrate.

distractorRationale.e: The stem explicitly says it is filtered.
distractorRationale.c: Secretion moves glucose in the opposite direction.
distractorRationale.a: The bladder does not perform that reaction.
